name: Prop Continuity

source.note: Standard production/script-supervision practice as much as a 'theory' -- included here because it's a concrete, highly checkable class of error once the knowledge graph exists.

definition: An object established as being in a character's possession, a specific location, or a specific state (broken, hidden, given away) should remain consistent with that state in later scenes unless a scene explicitly shows or implies it changing hands, location, or condition.
detection_signal: Using the knowledge graph's prop-mention index: track each significant prop's established location/owner/state across scenes in order. Flag contradictions (a character holding an object established as left behind, or destroyed, in an earlier scene, with no intervening scene explaining its return).
counter_considerations: Off-screen time skips can plausibly explain a prop's status changing without an on-page scene showing it — check for explicit time-skip markers before flagging as a hard contradiction; otherwise flag as lower-confidence.

name: Timeline Consistency
definition: Explicit or implicit time markers (day/night designations in scene headings, stated dates, references to elapsed time, characters' stated ages) should form a coherent, non-contradictory timeline across the script.
detection_signal: Using the knowledge graph: build a sequence of day/night designations and any explicit time references (INT./EXT. headers' time-of-day, dialogue references to dates/durations/ages). Flag contradictions (e.g. a 'DAY' scene immediately following a 'NIGHT' scene with dialogue implying no time has passed; a character's stated age shifting without a time skip).
counter_considerations: Non-linear narratives (flashbacks, intercut timelines, dream sequences) are a deliberate structure — the check needs to first establish whether the script uses a non-linear structure before treating an apparent contradiction as an error rather than an intentional cut.

name: Character Physical/Biographical Trait Continuity
definition: Physical descriptions and biographical facts established for a character (age, physical description, family relationships, hometown, occupation, name spelling) should remain consistent across all their appearances unless a scene explicitly addresses a change.
detection_signal: Using the knowledge graph's character-trait index: collect every explicit statement of a character's physical/biographical trait across the script. Flag direct contradictions (different stated ages without an explained time skip, an established sibling later referred to as a cousin, inconsistent name spelling in dialogue vs. scene headings).
counter_considerations: None of significance — this is one of the more purely mechanical, high-confidence checks in this knowledge base. A flagged contradiction here is very likely a genuine continuity error rather than an intentional narrative choice, though it's still worth a quick human confirmation.

name: World-Rule Consistency (Continuity Angle)

source.note: This is the same underlying principle as story_macro.json's world_rule_consistency, included here as well because it's operationally a knowledge-graph continuity check, not just a macro-thematic one -- the two entries share detection logic but serve different taxonomy purposes (macro trust vs. line-level contradiction detection).

definition: See world_rule_consistency in story_macro.json for the full theoretical framing. At the continuity level, the practical check is narrower: does any single explicit rule-statement directly contradict a later explicit event, independent of thematic considerations.
detection_signal: Using the knowledge graph: cross-reference explicit rule-establishing statements against explicit later events for direct logical contradiction.
counter_considerations: Same as world_rule_consistency: an acknowledged/consequential exception is not an error.
